title: Quibi's Leaders Shut It Down While There Was Money Left to Return
conflicts: Money raised: $1.75bn (AP/CBS, CNBC body, Engadget, Deadline Dec 2020, Tubefilter 2021) vs over $1.7bn (Deadline interview) vs $1.8bn (CFO.com/Crunchbase, Tubefilter 2020, Business Insider) vs nearly $2bn (Hollywood Reporter, CNBC summary) vs $1bn (Fox Business, apparently the first round); story uses $1.75bn. Cash left: about $350m (Deadline; WSJ via Engadget) and 'at least $350 million', with 'much more' to return (Whitman to CNBC); final amount returned not found, so the story says only that they chose to return what remained. Subscribers: ~500,000 (CNBC) vs 9.6m installs (Sensor Tower, not subscribers); story uses CNBC's figure, attributed.
notes: CNBC corrected that Meg Whitman was CEO, not a co-founder; the story calls Katzenberg the founder and Whitman the chief executive he recruited, and the founder field says so. Causes of failure are given only in the leaders' own words (idea, timing, pandemic); investor criticism reported by Deadline is not used. Quote stance complicates: Ben Sira on keeping faith with those who helped you, set against the fact that most of the money had already been spent.
